articleTitle: Optimum Sizing and Placement of Solar/Wind/Biogas Generating Units Using Dandelion Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: According to several studies, conventional fuels are a finite source of energy and have several negative effects on the environment. Therefore, it is in everyone's best interest to implement Distributed Generation Units based on renewable energy (or RDGs for short) to guarantee the proper operation of power systems. However, due to the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources and the fact that improper site selection of a photovoltaic (PV) or wind power plant cannot ensure optimal energy harvesting, the most efficient placement of the RDG units still poses a challenge. Additionally, the addition of biogas units will boost the effectiveness of electricity generation in agriculture-based countries with a large livestock population, along with solar PV and wind energy sources. In this study, an approach to ensure the optimal sizing and allocation of solar, biogas and wind powered units using the Dandelion Optimizer (DO) has been suggested where IEEE 69 bus has been used as a test case scenario. Comparative analysis has shown that the suggested algorithm performs better than other algorithms in this field, like the Pelican Optimizer Algorithm (POA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Equilibrium Optimizer (EO) where RDG units were introduced in the IEEE 69 bus system.

articleTitle: Triangular Current Modulations of DAB DC/DC Converter for Connecting PV Modules to DC Grid Considering Partial Shading
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Due to the wide range of Maximum Power Point (MPP) voltage of photovoltaic (PV) modules, high-voltage conversion ratio is desired from converters. Discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) modulations can bring high-voltage conversion ratio inherently. Hence, single-stage converters can become an option with DCM for such a high-voltage conversion application. In this paper, two triangular current modulations (TRM), which are named TRM1 and TRM2, are analyzed for the single-stage Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC/DC converter that converts PV energy under partial shading. During operations, TRM methods don’t require the knowledge of leakage inductance’s value which can vary under different current/temperature conditions. Hence, TRM methods have easier control versus hybrid current modulation (HCM). In addition, TRM methods have smaller magnetic core sizes versus conventional two-stage Boost Full-Bridge Isolated Converter (BFBIC). Hence, TRM methods of DAB DC/DC converter (especially TRM2 which serves smaller RMS currents) can be a good candidate for PV integration to DC grid.

articleTitle: Copper vs. Aluminum Windings in Dry-Type Transformers: A Comprehensive Study of Losses, Size, and Technical Attributes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Dry-type transformers are widely used in various applications, from power distribution systems to industrial units. A pivotal consideration in transformer design is the choice of conductor material, with copper and aluminum being the primary options. This manuscript presents a comprehensive experimental comparison between copper and aluminum windings in dry-type transformers, aiming to provide insights into their respective performance characteristics, efficiency, and weight. The study commences with a detailed overview of the properties and advantages of copper and aluminum as conductor materials. We explore factors such as electrical losses, and physical properties, which influence the efficiency, size, weight, and reliability of transformers. Using copper windings instead of aluminum in dry-type transformers for non-specific power needs does not offer any technical advantage. The thermal expansion coefficient of a copper conductor is less compatible with the resin than the aluminum conductor.

articleTitle: Testing Setup and Method to Characterize High-Force Shape Memory Alloy Wires
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper presents the determination of Shape Memory Alloy (SMA) wire parameters, their evolution and work limits. Thus, the two-way wires have been driven by electric current in the heating phase, with shape recovery being achieved by free cooling. In order to properly manage the temperature value, a proportional-integral (PI) controller was applied by the Simulink software, ESP32 development board and a double buck converter (DBC), which was accomplished with Arduino Uno R3 development board as the driving unit of the MOSFET power transistors. In this way, the displacement, force and reaction time of the wires were determined. The values of the parameters are important to provide specialists valuable information, and allow adequate implementation of the SMA elements in actuators or other electromechanical devices and applications. Tests resulted in a relatively high-force of the SMA wires, a good stability in displacement, and the possibility to use them instead of the pneumatic or hydraulic pistons, in certain applications.

articleTitle: Dimensioning a Photovoltaic System Based on the Coverage of Own Electricity Consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The development of renewable energy sources is a priority both for the Republic of Moldova and internationally. The Republic of Moldova is 80% dependent on the import of electricity, which has led the decision-makers to adopt policies to support the development of renewable energy sources. In Moldova there are 3 support schemes for renewable energy producers. One of the support schemes is net metering intended for consumers to cover their own electricity consumption. Correct sizing of the photovoltaic system is a decisive factor for the investment recovery period. The paper includes an analysis regarding the choice of the photovoltaic system installed power for different types of consumers in the Republic of Moldova, using a main criteria coverage of the own electricity consumption. The data reflected in this paper are based on real cases, measured and collected from potential beneficiaries of photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Effects of Gap Length of a Step Lap Joint on the No Load Losses of Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This work mainly focuses on the study of the effect of the gap between joints in the step-lap joints of the core, where the magnetic flux density and no-load losses related to the configuration of the step-lap joint are considered. Both the narrow and wide gaps between the step-lap joint are examined to evaluate the no-load losses and magnetic flux distribution. To investigate the effect of the average magnetic flux density on the no-load losses and magnetic flux distribution with different gap lengths, several levels of the magnetic flux density (from 0.05 to 2 T) have been examined. Numerical results illustrate that low losses can be achieved by using a narrow gap between the joints. The results also show that the difference in the no-load losses between the different gaps after 1.5 T decreased significantly.

articleTitle: An Estimate of the Operating Time of a Li-Ion Battery for Supplying a Three-Phase Power Converter With a Dynamic Random Load
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: It is a methodology that approaches an estimated evolution of the operating time, for a converter that uses a Li-Ion battery. The conversion system is very close to a real one, where the functional blocks in the simulator are found in mass-produced electronic devices. Their functional parameters and yield are just initialization values for the simulation. The system's adaptability for real operation turns into a case study for electronic devices or modules. The conversion of electricity from DC to three-phase AC starts from the Li-Ion battery charged to a certain percentage of the SOC (State of charge) indicator. The discharge of the battery, depending on a variable electrical load, will be calculated and estimated following a monitoring process for the converter.The electric power evolution function is determined by memorized and correlated evolutions with random generators. Estimating an operating time becomes a possible problem even if the mode of variation of the load is random.

articleTitle: Implementation of Dijkstra and Floyd-Warshall Algorithms in Dynamic Dimensioning and 3D Geospatial Positioning Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a communication protocol for wireless networks operating in the 2.4GHz frequency band. This protocol aims to alleviate data traffic congestion among mobile platforms and optimize the dataset that needs to be relayed within the network. The communication protocol employs the Dijkstra and Floyd-Warshall algorithms, known for finding the shortest path, thereby structuring the sensor network into a tree or graph, where nodes are represented by mobile platforms. This protocol is utilized in wireless ad-hoc sensor networks

articleTitle: Analysis of the Electric Field Strength Emitted by Wireless Devices Operating at 868.3 MHz in the Vicinity of the Human Body
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The aim of this article is to investigate the impact of the electric field emitted by an antenna operating at a frequency of 868.3 MHz on the human body. The operating frequency falls within the radiofrequency range and was chosen due to its widespread use in various wireless communication systems, such as smart building and security systems. This simulation was conducted using the COMSOL Multiphysics software and was performed in the Radio Frequency, Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (EMW). The elements that compose this simulation are: the human body, the signal-emitting antenna and the enclosure. Within the simulation, it has been observed that the equipment operating at the 868.3 MHz frequency emits a low electric field strength near the human body, that has a non-hazardous impact under safe conditions.

articleTitle: Grey Wolf Optimizer Algorithm to Solve Optimal Placement and Sizing of the Distributed Generation Sources in Distribution Radial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Electric power utilities are paying a lot of attention right now to the optimal placement and sizing of distributed generation (DG) a at the radial distribution grids for the goal of minimizing real power loss. Power loss minimization has several built-in advantages, such as the feeder lines power flow will be reducing, relieving stress on feeder loading to extend their life, increasing the possibility of using the current facility to meet any increase in load demand, avoiding the need to buy power from the grid and saving money on loss compensating equipment, lowering customer bills, etc. In this paper, the optimal placement and size of distributed generation (DG) units will be addressed using one of the most popular metaheuristics optimization techniques namely the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO). The main aim of this paper is minimized the real power losses on distribution network and improved the voltage profiles and enhanced the voltage stability index by adding DG units on optimal location and determine the optimal sizing with satisfied the equality and inequality constrains. The approach proposed determining the optimal placement by reconfiguring the DG on all buses and calculating the real power losses. The optimal placement is achieved on a bus with the lowest real power losses. The optimal sizing of the DG unit can be achieved by using Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO). GWO is a meta-heuristics optimization technique inspired by the social behavior of grey wolves. The IEEE 33 bus radial system will be tested to prove the superiority and efficiency of the proposed algorithm. According to the simulation results that were obtained and the evaluation of the various cases that were taken into consideration, the placement of DG units results in a large loss reduction with a favorable voltage profile as well as the line loading in the power distribution networks is released.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Practical Study of the Effect of DC Grid Wire Temperature Variation on Transmission Losses
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The ohmic resistance of DC lines causes losses during power transmission while variations in conductor temperature change the resistance accordingly. Typically, the resistances of specific wires mentioned in technical documentation correspond to some constant reference temperature which is usually 20°C. It was therefore decided to analyze the effect of the temperature of overhead catenary wires on the amount of transmission losses and total energy consumption in the case of trolleybus motion by means of simulations and calculations. In the practical part, an experimental study was performed to investigate how the voltage drop on DC lines increases due to temperature increase when an electricity consumer is operated at constant power.

articleTitle: Implementation of SHEPWM Based on Particle Swarm Optimization in a Two-Level Three-phase Inverter Using dSPACE DS1104 Controller Board
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This research study provides the analysis, simulation, and experimental investigation of selective harmonic elimination with pulse width modulation for three phase inverter using the particle swarm optimization method. By employing this modulation technique, the inverter output voltage will be improved while the switching components' lifespan will be increased. The paper presents the harmonic issue in an analytical manner. The dSPACE DS1104 controller board, a digital signal processor, has been used with the MATLAB environment to verify the method's correctness. The experimental results closely approximate the simulation findings, supporting earlier studies about the efficiency of the particle swarm optimization based selective harmonic elimination.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Water Extraction in an Electrostatic Wire-Cylinder System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Concerning the increasing need to control humidity or efficiently collect and retain water from the air in various applications, phase-change heat exchangers are typically used for these purposes, operating at low temperatures below the dew point to facilitate the condensation of water vapor. However, it should be considered that the energy required for cooling the condenser in such devices can become significant regarding their primary functions. This paper presents an experimental study concerning the implementation of an enhanced electrostatic phase-change rate water condenser with a wire-cylinder design. This improvement is achieved by promoting the nucleation of water vapor and fine droplets on mobile charge carriers generated through corona discharge. Furthermore, the electric field pushes water vapors and droplets toward the cooled condenser wall. Water droplets and vapor are studied in terms of additional potential introduced to the evaporation energy barrier on the surface of the droplets through dielectrophoretic interactions with charge carriers. The experimental results on the phase-change effect of the corona discharge reveal a significant improvement of at least 15% in condensation rate.

articleTitle: Using Analog Complex Mixers for Low-IF Mixing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: IQ mixers and complex mixers are both used to cancel the image band signal. In this paper, we analyse a complex IF sub-THz receiver architecture aimed for splitting a multi-GHz baseband signal into narrower sub-bands for easier A/D conversion. The architecture consists of a normal IQ direct downconversion, followed by complex mixers to center the chosen sub-carriers to DC. Image rejection versus mismatch errors is calculated both analytically and on system and circuit-level simulations. It was seen that the image rejection is dominated by the IQ downconversion stage. It is demonstrated that the mismatches in the IQ stage can be corrected digitally by weighted summing of the digital sub-bands.

articleTitle: Modeling of Static Force Characteristic of a Bistable Permanent Magnet Actuator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this work is presented modeling of static force characteristic of a bistable permanent magnet actuator. Finite element method model has been used. Results for steady-state force operational characteristic are calculated and presented. Relations of force to air-gap characteristics with power supply are calculated and presented. Discussion on energy efficiency improvement and force enhancement considerations are made.

articleTitle: A Brief Technical Analysis of Energy Sector in Romania Based on Renewables Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The adoption of the Paris Agreement at the Climate Change Conference (COP21) on December 12<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> 2015 marks an emblematic date in the fight against climate change. The Paris Agreement was signed by 196 countries, including Romania, and came into force on November 4, 2016. In order to fulfill the requirements of the agreement, the European Union has signed the European Green Deal, its targets being ambitious, which will turn the European Union into a prosperous economy, very efficient in terms of the use of all resources. In support of the successful implementation of the European Green Deal in 2021, through the " Fit for 55 " package, European Union has come up with a series of legislative and policy measures to increase the share of green energy in the European Union's energy mix by up to 40%.The purpose of the paper is to analyze the energy potential of Romania in relation to energy from renewable sources. Moreover, in this article is briefly presented the current stage of battery energy storage systems, the technology being relatively new in Romania.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modeling of a Probe for Scanning Microwave Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This work presents a model of an electromagnetic scanning microwave microscope cantilever used for a microwave probe. Real size high frequency model is designed and used in the frequency range 8 – 12 GHz. The aim is to look at the interaction of the scanning electromagnetic waves with different surface materials, such as metallic conductors and semiconductor materials. Results for electromagnetic field distributions are calculated for base scanning surfaces such as Si, GaAs and Au solid plates. Results obtained are useful for improving measurement accuracy of electromagnetic scanning microwave microscopy method in the case of electrically conductive surfaces.

articleTitle: Hydrometeorological Buoy with Real-Time Data Transmission to Maritime Hydrographic Directorate
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The project "Hydrometeorological buoy with real-time data transmission" aims to create a modern, educational model for recording and transmitting hydrometeorological data in marine areas, benefiting the Maritime Hydrographic Directorate for real-time weather and water condition monitoring. The project used electronic components like an Arduino Uno board and specialized sensors to measure various parameters, a GSM module for data transmission via SMS, and a sustainable, solar-powered external battery for the buoy. The buoy's housing was constructed from biodegradable, golden-colored material designed in Autodesk Fusion360 and produced using a 3D printer.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of a Flexible Wireless High Power Charging System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper deals with the numerical simulation of a flexible wireless high power system for charging the batteries of electric vehicles. The key component that ensures the contactless power transfer and interoperability is the inductive coupler. Its parameters depend on the transmitter and receiver coils structure, magnetic cores material and shape, distance between them etc. The parameters of the inductive coupler were determined by a 3D finite element analysis using Flux® software package and they were further used for numerical simulation of the entire charging system using Matlab/Simulink® environment. The numerical simulations were carried out for battery charging of a heavy duty electric vehicle (e.g. electric bus or truck) and of a commercial electric vehicle. Stray fields were also computed to verify their compliance with the values imposed by international standards.

Author Keywords: heavy duty and commercial electric vehicles

articleTitle: Efficiency Comparison of Discharge Strategies of Mobile Supercapacitor Energy Storage System for Public Electric Transport
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper analyses and compares three discharge strategies for a mobile supercapacitor energy storage system of public electric transport – trolleybus. Within each strategy, the trolleybus traction drive is supplied with power from both overhead DC catenary and supercapacitors during the entire acceleration mode. According to the simulation results, these strategies are nearly equivalent in terms of efficiency when comparing the total energy consumptions of the catenary supply substation. On the other hand, it was found that strategies or cases where supercapacitors get discharged before the end of the acceleration mode should be avoided because during this phase the drive consumes the highest power due to which also overhead transmission losses are higher thus resulting up to 5% reduction in efficiency of supercapacitor energy storage system using.

articleTitle: The Analysis of the Airgap and Geometry for the Calculation of the Torque on a Stepper Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper aims to present the analysis of various airgap values for the detent and holding torques calculation for a hybrid stepper motor using FEM analysis. The stepper motors are designed considering all the technical performances stated in the Technical specification must be fulfilled. For this, the numerical analysis using three–dimensional modeling is intensively used in the design stage to calculate detent and holding torques versus angle characteristics. An experimental model for the stepper motor is presented, also. The parasitic and holding torque versus angle are shown, and the calculated and measured values are compared.

articleTitle: A Faster Algorithm For Frequency Solving Of Nonlinear Three-Phase Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The Hănţilă Method is successfully used for solving nonlinear problems in electrical engineering, including nonlinear three-phase circuits. The method is highly versatile and allows the analysis of many harmonics. In this paper, we analyze a new approach to accelerate it. This involves modifying the algorithm by removing the computation of the Fourier series coefficients from the iterative cycle. This is achieved by calculating the transfer characteristic of the linear part of the algorithm. During an iteration computations are performed only in the time domain. The duration of an iteration is no longer affected by an increase in the number of analyzed harmonics. Thus, they can notably increase without significantly affecting the computation time.

articleTitle: The Improvement of Model Performance for Automated Tooth Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Automated tooth identification has been an emerging research topic in the field of dental research in recent years. It has a critical importance for dental health records, forensic dentistry and even age estimation. Instead of conventional methods, modern artificial intelligence techniques, like deep learning, have a significant potential for automatic recognition towards digital dentistry. This work aims to classify the type of teeth which are categorized into four different classes, incisor, canine, premolar and molar, using deep learning models. Cropped images of publicly available Tufts Dental Database, x-ray panoramic radiography image dataset, is used to train and test the models. It proposes modifications on the CNNs (Convolutional Neural Networks), namely ResNet152 and MobileNetV2 to get more robust and accurate results. The effect of neural network depth, convolution kernel size and residual blocks are investigated in the backbone of the network. Model performances are evaluated by confusion matrix, resulting in accuracy, precision and recall. MobileNetV2 yielded the highest accuracy of 84.25%. When the number of convolution layers is increased, it is observed that the classification performance improves more than the other two parameters. Automated tooth identification represents a significant advancement in the fields of dentistry and even forensics, streamlining the process of matching dental records and enhancing accuracy and efficiency in identifying individuals based on their dental characteristics.

articleTitle: Software Tools for Signal and Data Analysis Using LabView Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The solutions for the computerized integration, control and management of all the (vital) functions of some technical installations, aim to reduce administrative and maintenance costs, to increase the efficiency and comfort of the occupants and to improve business performance in general. Signal processing is one of the most studied domains as, in real life, the distances between the signal generation and the decision unit can be important. Also, the generation of the signal at the source is not without additional noise. For example, when controlling electric powertrains, this noise can be a source of errors. The possibility of creating commands that destabilize the vehicle is not far off. In this context, the present paper proposes few ways, tools and examples that are able to generate signals and noises. The result is displayed to observe signal evolution without or with the influence of other processes. The examples are built using National Instruments' graphical programming environment, LabVIEW.

articleTitle: The Study on the Implementation of High-Power Photovoltaic Systems on Military Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper is part of a comprehensive study aimed at powering a military platform with electricity generated through photovoltaic panels. The current work focuses on the theoretical aspects and simulating the electricity generation process, with future plans to disseminate information regarding the practical implementation of the project. The simulation was conducted using the PvSyst software, a recognized tool for simulation and analysis in the field of solar energy. Providing green energy to a military platform not only grants it energy independence but also reduces its carbon footprint. This effort contributes to global initiatives aimed at combating climate change by lowering CO2 emissions. This initiative represents a significant step towards a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: Determination of Cognitive-Emotional Characteristics through the Method of Individual Asymmetries of Power Spectral Density of EEG Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Understanding an individual's cognitive and emotional state is crucial for analyzing their psychological characteristics and behaviors and diagnosing and treating mental health disorders. This research is especially relevant today, as the World Health Organization reports that 15-20% of the world's population suffers from a mental health disorder, and 25% experience one in their lifetime. Early identification of these conditions is essential for creating effective treatment plans and assessing their impact. This study focuses on the analysis of EEG (electroencephalogram) waves, a standard method for determining stress levels, anxiety, depression, behavior, and personality characteristics. Such studies have broad implications for fields like neuroscience, data science, Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), and Artificial Intelligence (AI), as they aim to understand how the human brain functions regarding sensory, motor, cognitive, and emotional aspects. In this article, we introduce an EEG wave analysis method that can serve as the basis for a clustering or classification algorithm in machine learning. By leveraging EEG data, we contribute to the ongoing efforts to enhance our understanding of human cognition and emotion, ultimately facilitating early detection and treatment of mental health conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel Computational Approach for Estimating the Side Lobe Peaks in Non-Uniformly Spaced Linear Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Optimization of linear antenna arrays with the non-uniformly spaced elements has enticed many researchers and a plethora of literature is available on this subject. This topic received further attention due to the growth of 5G technology and Internet of Things (IoT). This paper presents a restructured mathematical expression of the antenna array factor, for estimating the side lobe peaks. An objective function incorporating the proposed atypical expression is framed and is employed for improved side-lobe reduction using the Genetic Algorithm (GA). The alternate expression for array factor bequeaths with the endowment to predict the angles at which the side lobe peaks occur, thereby curtailing the computational complexity when incorporated by the GA to minimize the side lobes. Simulations are performed for optimizing the radiation pattern using the GA for varying array sizes and for varying constraints on the array inter-element spacing. A comparison of the results affirms the effectiveness of the proposed expression in terms of side-lobe reduction and improved computational efficiency. The proposed expression can be incorporated with other evolutionary algorithms to optimize the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: LP 8T SRAM: Design of New Technique SRAM With Reduced Power Consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In the landscape of VLSI design, where memory hierarchy plays a pivotal role, two pressing challenges take center stage: power dissipation and propagation delay. The primary goal of the research is to craft a low-power SRAM tailored for the demands of 16nm technology. Leveraging the 16nm PTM model for PMOS and NMOS components, the approach aims to usher in an era of efficient semiconductor design. The SRAM design achieves a remarkable reduction in power consumption without compromising on acceptable propagation delay and maintaining a compact physical footprint. Recognizing the vital role SRAM plays in the intricate memory hierarchy, the approach diligently tailors the method to ensure that power gating becomes an integral component in the conventional SRAM design, leading to substantial enhancements in power efficiency and signal delay. A comprehensive series of simulations and analyses, conducted with the aid of LTspice, serves to validate the effectiveness of the innovative approach, promising a brighter future for electronic devices. As a significant contribution to the evolution of these devices, the work stands as a valuable milestone in the quest for efficiency and excellence in the world of VLSI design.

articleTitle: Magnetohydrodynamic Induced Separation in Liquid Filled Magnetic Gaps of Surface Mounted Permanent Magnet Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: An intriguing phenomenon has been observed following an extended test validation run of a permanent magnet motor with liquid filled magnetic gap. There were noticed traces of localized deposits on both ends of the shaft and corresponding discoloration areas on the carbon fiber-PEEK (Polyether Ether Ketone) sleeve of the permanent magnet rotor. We propose a magnetohydrodynamics, electrochemical model. The forensic tests performed on the deposits show a high level of consistency with the proposed model.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation Study on Board Ships
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper presents the results of electromagnetic measurements of a maritime ship. The data was gathered in the areas outside the ship metal structure (three unshielded areas) and inside the vessel (a shielded area). Additional screens were used to protect the personnel as well as the electro-energetic and communications equipment. The field level on board the ship was measured according to the frequency bands. The values were compared with those of the standards in force, taking into account that the radiation of the emitters represents a risk for the health of the personnel on board. The levels of the electric field and power density in the four areas were presented. Measurements were made with and without shielding during the operation of three communications equipment. Function of ship size and shape of it, the location of the communication equipment and their type, the influence of the electric field level on the crew was analyzed.

articleTitle: Thermal Images Based Mobile Application for Identifying Faults in Photovoltaics Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper describes few faults that can be present in Photovoltaic modules and presents results related to training and the testing of a mobile application designed for identifying faults in photovoltaic modules based on thermal images. The mobile application was trained and then tested with different individual and multiple faults. The mobile application can identify with high accuracy both the individual and multiple faults if the thermal images are preprocessed before to be uploaded for analysis.

articleTitle: Inclusivity in Electronic Communication: A Morse Code Interface for Visual and Auditory Deficiencies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper addresses the communication needs of individuals with both visual and auditory deficiencies and proposes an inclusive electronic communication interface. Recognizing the limitations faced by this limited group, we present a solution that harnesses the efficiency and versatility of Morse Code. The suggested didactic models consisting of an embedded device and a Graphical User Interface design are tailored to simplify user experience and offer a comprehensive and accessible means of electronic communication between individuals, and with electronic devices. The solution not only addresses existing technological gaps but also fosters greater inclusivity in the realm of electronic communication and offers many further development directions in the areas of Smart-Home design. This research strives to contribute to the advancement of technology with a focus on enhancing accessibility and usability for individuals facing combined visual and auditory impairments.

articleTitle: A Gamification Software to Aid Students to Perform Better at Exams
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Based on the literature it’s possible to affirm that gamification helps students to have better results in education than conventional methods. In order to apply this methodology, the electrical engineering department at UNISATC in South of Brazil, developed a gamification tool called Electric Game. The development of this tool started in 2018 and since then, it has helped students with the National Performance Exam (ENADE). In the beginning this game was played manually and then it evolved to digital to avoid problems such as long waiting times during the checking process. This brought agility to the process and allowed them to identify information about student’s performance, as well as enabling remote access for students and teachers. This paper will present the main developments of this tool in addition to the results of a case study.

articleTitle: Modelling of Linear Coils Using Arduino Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper describes a modelling approach for linear coils based on Arduino Uno platform. As such, there is the possibility to analyze multi-module systems with complex architectures such as electrical drive systems or other automation systems, not necessarily electrical, but which are currently found in plenty in the industrial domain. At the same time, from a financial point of view, there is no need to spend money on the purchase of real equipment. The design of complex systems, including closed-loop ones, is performed with less resources and faster due to the flexibility of the method, i.e., specific mathematical models are customized to fit each device. Models are defined by ordinary differential equations solved by numerical methods. Other equipment classes can also be modelled using the described approach, not just electromagnetic ones.

articleTitle: Improvement of Load Frequency Control of Multi-Sources Power System Based on PID Controller Using Particle Swarm Optimization with Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Load Frequency Control (LFC) is an essential part of the power system network because it guarantees the frequency constraints at normal conditions after a load perturbation. The main factors of stability that should be taken into account in the power system networks are the frequency deviations of each area and the amount of power flow through the tie-line interconnected power system. These indicators must be kept at the desired levels based on the application of controllers. This article designs load frequency control based on a simple, robust, and powerful algorithm to modify the frequency limits and improve the power delivery of multi-source power system networks by making optimization tuning for the parameters of the PID controller using the particle swarm optimization technique. This algorithm is more reliable in achieving the lowest objective function, where the Integral Time Multiplied Absolute Error (ITAE) is used as the objective function in this paper, hence improving the response of the system (steady-state frequency deviation, rise time, peak time, settling time, and peak amplitude).

articleTitle: Time-Variable Mutual Inductance for Enhanced Inductive Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Enhanced inductive power transmission (IPT) between coaxially arranged circular coils is introduced by timemodulation of the mutual inductance. This modulation is accomplished by coherent switching of the short circuit current induced in a third loop. An analytical circuit model supporting the design for future time-modulated IPT systems is derived. We demonstrate an increase in load rms-voltage by 13% (28% gain in power) compared to an unmodulated transfer on an experimental system operating at fundamental frequencies ranging from 40 kHz to 500 kHz.

articleTitle: Modeling of the Inductive Heating Process of a Cylindrical Part at Two Different Frequencies, in Order to Optimize a Process of Joining an Assembly of Parts Made of Different Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The work is focused on a study that refers to the distribution of the electromagnetic and thermal field in a metallic structure subjected to the heating process by inductive methods. In order to optimize the electrotechnological process, two frequencies of the power supply are considered in the paper. The work presented will be a first stage of a more complex study regarding the use of inductive heating in joining processes of structures made of different metallic materials.

articleTitle: The Fault Working Regimes of the Six-Phase Symmetrically Wound Asynchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper is focused on the study of six-phase asynchronous motors with symmetrical stator winding with some possible supply faults. The description of the working regimes of the six-phase asynchronous machine with 6, 5, 4 and 3-phase power supply is based on the mathematical model of the magnetomotive force (MMF) in the air gap. To confirm the theoretical results, several experimental tests of the six-phase asynchronous motor with the symmetrical stator winding were carried out. Also, the degree of tolerance of the power supply interruption of some phases was determined. The obtained results can be used to adjust the control and protection system of the six-phase asynchronous motor for normal operation and when faults occur.

articleTitle: Security Risk Assessment of Electricity Supply at 220/110/20 kV Sardanesti Power Substation from Romania
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The assessment of the security risk of electricity supply to industrial and household consumers within the National Power System, comes in the context in which the possibility of a blackout is very likely, and the lack of electricity can cause major damage through enormous financial losses, which through the domino effect can spread economic and national insecurity. In this context, the risk assessment of the security of electricity supply to industrial consumers becomes an essential issue of national security and makes this paper of real interest. As known in the literature, the 400 kV and 220 kV power substations within the National Power Grid Transelectrica, are listed as critical power infrastructures and for this reason this paper requires essential multidisciplinary, interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary knowledge of power engineering, industrial engineering, security and protection of critical power infrastructures and energy security. The essential and interesting elements brought in this risk analysis are: determining the probability of the chosen risk scenario, determining the severity, calculation of the risk matrix and elaboration of the energy security strategy on the power substation in this paper. The authors consider that the security of electricity supply to consumers within the National Power System is a strictly national and european security issue because the lack of electricity can cause enormous damage to the industry, economy and state systems, which are almost entirely dependent on electricity.

articleTitle: Novel Application of Hurst Exponent and Fractal Analysis for Predictive Maintenance in Electric Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This research proposal introduces a novel approach to predictive maintenance in electric generators by leveraging the Hurst exponent and fractal analysis. The aim is to enhance the reliability and efficiency of electric generators used in critical infrastructure by analyzing operational data. By quantifying the long-term behavior and fractal characteristics of generator operations, this research seeks to determine failure rates and optimize maintenance intervals.

articleTitle: Water-Cooled Free Rare-Earth Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor - Design and Practical Implementation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper presents the design and practical implementation of a series of permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motors. Aspects such as design characteristics, electromagnetic simulation, LAB analysis, efficiency investigation, and testing bench presentation during different manufacturing steps are discussed. The motor benefits from free rare earth magnets, and to increase the efficiency and to maintain imposed geometrical specifications, the water-cooling thermal design was selected. Experimental verifications of testing the motor class proved the validity of the proposed machines.

Author Keywords: permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor

articleTitle: Efficient Frequency Domain Models for Simulation of Circuits with Diode Rectifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper proposes some efficient frequency domain (FD) models of circuits whose nonlinear elements consist in half wave (one diode) and full wave (two diodes) rectifiers. This class of circuits may contain a lot of home appliances (air conditioners, vacuum cleaners, refrigerators, microwave ovens, washing machines) together with various lightning devices such as LEDs and CFLs driven by electronic circuits. All these devices contain the above diode rectifiers. The analyses using the proposed models lead to a shorter simulation time than that used by TRAN or various HB analyses implemented in ADS.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of a Linear Induction Motor for Electromagnetic Launchers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper deals with the design and analysis of a three phase linear induction motor integrated in an electromagnetic launcher of small size drones. The moving part of the machine is an aluminum plate (which the drone is attached to) that is rapidly accelerated to the target speed, over a short distance. Different quantities are calculated such as magnetic flux density distribution and equi-flux lines, propulsion force, speed and position of the armature etc. A parametric analysis is also carried out and its purpose is to estimate the influence of several geometric and electric parameters (thickness and length of aluminum plate, air-gap length, frequency) on the system performance. Electromagnetic field computations based on finite element method are carried out to estimate the performance of the linear motor in various scenarios using the software package Flux ®.

articleTitle: Enhanced Loss Function for the Design of Image Transform Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have triggered important progress in image-to-image mapping. The enhanced learning capabilities allow them to understand the input visual layout and perform local transformations customized to image content. This paper discusses an approach based on Generative Adversarial Convolutional Neural Networks (GAN) to help augment training datasets with generated images. The proposed design uses a loss function that integrates terms based on image quality metrics to validate the production of realistic images. This allows the configuration of neural parameters according to the visual perception of the generated images, without imposing a strict pixel-wise similarity with targets. This technique could be helpful for real applications in which supervised training should be done for pairs of input-output images that do not illustrate the same scene. The performance of the proposed approach is illustrated by a transformation of outdoor scenes from summer to winter. The experiments performed for different GAN schemes and quality metrics show improved quality of the generated images when the loss function includes loss terms related to visual perception.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Prosumers on the Low-Voltage Electrical Distribution Networks Based on a Scenarios-Based Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper proposes a methodology to assess the impact of the increase in the number of prosumers in the lowvoltage electrical distribution networks from the point of view of energy losses and voltage levels. A real low-voltage electrical distribution network belonging to a Romanian Distribution Network Operator has been used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The final results indicated a threshold of the prosumers' penetration degree of 20% (percentage from the total number of the end-users connected to the network) without additional measures to increase the hosting capacity of the network, corresponding to the minimum energy losses and the integration of all phase voltages between the admissible limits, indicated in the performance standard for the electricity distribution service, at the end-user's level. The methodology allow incorporation of the strategies based on technical measures integrating load balancing and voltage control algorithms and resizing of the conductors, which will increase the penetration degree.

articleTitle: Memory Management Strategies for an Internet of Things System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The rise of the Internet has brought about significant changes in our lives, and the rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) is poised to have an even more substantial impact by connecting a wide range of devices across various application domains. IoT devices, especially low-end ones, are constrained by limited memory and processing capabilities, necessitating efficient memory management within IoT operating systems. This paper delves into the importance of memory management in IoT systems, with a primary focus on the design and configuration of such systems, as well as the scalability and performance of scene management. Effective memory management is critical for optimizing resource usage, responsiveness, and adaptability as the IoT ecosystem continues to grow. The study offers insights into memory allocation, scene execution, memory reduction, and system scalability within the context of an IoT system, ultimately highlighting the vital role that memory management plays in facilitating a seamless and efficient IoT experience.

articleTitle: The Impact of Electric Arc Furnaces on the Cuban Power System: Existing Approaches and Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this paper, a detailed analysis of the main electrical problems arising in the Cuban electrical system because of the operation of electric arc furnaces is made. It also provides an overview of the solutions that have been taken in the steel mills to mitigate some of these problems and analyzes the remaining technical issues. Using simulation results, several solutions are analyzed individually, from the perspective of the different electrical problems, justifying each variant with conditions very similar to the real ones of the Cuban electrical system.

articleTitle: A Novel Energy-Efficient and Scalable Clustering-Based Routing Protocol for 3D Under Water Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs) play a crucial role in various aquatic applications, such as environmental monitoring, underwater exploration, and disaster management. One of the major challenges in UWSNs is the limited energy resources of underwater sensor nodes, which necessitates the development of energy-efficient routing protocols to extend network lifetime. This paper introduces a novel clustering-based routing protocol designed specifically for UWSNs to address this challenge. The proposed clustered-based routing protocol, namely Energy-Efficient Scalable Clustering Protocol (EESCP), leverages the benefits of clustering to prolong network lifetime while ensuring scalability and adaptability to dynamically varying environments of UWSN. EESCP employs a multi-hop communication strategy between source and sink to minimize energy consumption with the objective of prolonging the lifetime of underwater sensor nodes. The protocol adapts to changing network conditions by allowing cluster reconfiguration when needed, ensuring robustness and scalability. To evaluate the performance of EESCP, we conducted extensive simulations in various underwater scenarios. The proposed protocol is compared with some of the benchmark protocols such as LEACH, MH-LEACH, SHEENA, etc. The results demonstrate that EESCP outperforms these benchmark protocols.
